SMTO-MEM-0021 — SMTO couldn't rebuild search data for some documents

GUID: 1afb7f99-fbed-5d70-b052-bab3dea98afb
Slug: knowledge-index-restore-failed
Domain: MEM · Subsystem: knowledge

What happened

  • Search data for some documents was missing, and SMTO's earlier try at rebuilding it from saved copies failed. Those documents can't be searched until they are indexed again.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Look at the status line at the top of Knowledge. If it says document search is unavailable, select Check again, or ask your administrator to repair it. Rebuilding needs the search service running; while it's down, every rebuild fails.
  2. Open the conversation or collection that holds the documents and, on each one, select Manage, then Reindex. Reindex reads the original file again and builds fresh search data, instead of repeating the failed rebuild.
  3. Open Test retrieval and search for text you know is in those documents. Passages from them confirm the new search data works.

What success looks like

  • The documents show Ready to search, and Test retrieval returns their passages.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't delete the documents; their original files are needed to rebuild the search data.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Document search hit a missing vector index, but the restore job for that document generation had already failed, so the search reported index_restore_failed instead of queuing another restore.

What this means

  • The app could not restore the saved search data. Keep the original documents so their search data can be rebuilt. The original operation and completed work retain their own recorded outcomes; this diagnostic does not replay them.

Why this can happen

  • The component reported index_restore_failed. This does not establish the outcome of unrelated operations.

How to diagnose it

  • The restored or rebuilt index reaches Ready.
  • Inspect the error reference and the affected component’s current observation before selecting a recovery action.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the failed restore job (identity restore:document:generation) in /api/agent/rag/jobs and the Server log for its cause, such as a missing generation record or passages file, or a vector database or embedding failure. Fix that cause, then Reindex the affected documents to build a new generation from the original source.
  • Keep the original sources and ask an administrator to inspect Knowledge’s installation status. Reindex affected sources after the service is available.

Retry and execution caution

  • The restored or rebuilt index reaches Ready.

How to verify the fix

  • The restored or rebuilt index reaches Ready.

What not to do

  • Do not delete retained task data or repeat an operation with an unknown outcome.

Technical notes

  • Status checks do not replay tasks or modify source documents.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
